messages:
ashley: quick heads-up — ran a cross-model hybrid quant sweep tonight (llama-3b, mistral-7b, qwen-7b) against the new kernel selector + batching heuristic. posting raw notes here so we have a single thread.

sam: awesome, thanks. what changed in the selector?

ashley: selector now considers: model_arch, avg_req_seq, prefix_length_histogram, and a soft cost delta from quant calibration. we also added a small hysteresis window to avoid flipping kernels on short prefixes.

jin: did you include kv-cache retention/aliasing in the heuristics? that's been a big source of surprises.

ashley: yes — we track kv_cache_reuse_ratio per-route and penalize kernel switches that would require a KV layout copy if reuse_ratio > 0.25. that avoided one class of stalls.

maria: numbers? latency and p50/p99 comparisons?

ashley: paste of the main table compressed:

```
Model      | Profile      | p50 (ms)  | p95 (ms)  | p99 (ms)  | tokens/sec
llama-3b   | fp8-opt      | 9.6       | 26.5      | 54.3      | 880
llama-3b   | int8-fallback| 11.8      | 34.1      | 75.0      | 680
mistral-7b | fp8-opt      | 14.2      | 42.0      | 98.5      | 540
qwen-7b    | hybrid-4/8   | 16.1      | 48.9      | 110.2     | 500
```

Note: fp8-opt uses fp8 kernels everywhere that passed calibration; hybrid-4/8 is int4 where safe + fp8 on attention.

perf-bot: alert: llama-3b fp8-opt had a 12% throughput regression on long-prefix scenario compared to yesterday's baseline (run 1977769000).

sam: where's the regression coming from? kernel swap overhead?

ashley: looked into traces — it's KV copy spikes when sequence length crosses 256. kernel selector was switching from fp8_kv_aligned to fp8_kv_copy variant at that boundary. the copy path serializes kv layout for the new kernel and stalls other in-flight tokens.

jin: can we avoid the copy by aligning kernels to the canonical kv layout? maybe add a constraint to prefer kernels with compatible kv format when next_kv_op_prob > 0.6

ashley: attempted that; it reduces copies but increases avg p50 slightly because the preferred kernel is a bit slower on short prefixes. tradeoff between p50 and p99.

maria: any quality delta from fp8 calibration? was top-1/roundtrip eval checked?

ashley: did BLEU/ROUGE-lite on a sanity set — no meaningful regressions for llama and mistral at fp8-opt. qwen hybrid showed a few tokenization edgecases (0.3% higher repetition) when int4 applied to FFN layers with alpha<0.02.

devex: is this a blocker for rollout? customers on dedicated could see p99 regressions.

ashley: not immediate blocker — can enable new selector behind a feature flag and restrict auto-switching by default for dedicated tiers. plan: roll to staging, soak 48h, then canary 5% prod routes.

sam: configs you used? can you paste the exact quant/profile config we ran so we can reproduce?

ashley: here's the run config snippet:

```
quant_profile:
  name: field-sweep-2026-03
  rules:
    - model: llama-3b
      prefer: fp8_kv_aligned
      fallback: int8_basic
      switch_hysteresis_ms: 250
    - model: mistral-7b
      prefer: fp8_kv_copy
      kv_copy_penalty: 0.35
    - model: qwen-7b
      prefer: hybrid_int4_ffn_fp8_attn
      int4_threshold: 0.015
selector:
  score_weights:
    latency: 0.5
    kv_copy_penalty: 0.3
    quality_risk: 0.2
  min_switch_uptime_ms: 2000
  batch_align: 8
```

jin: small note — batch_align 8 causes padding for many small requests. observed a 4% effective throughput loss on tails. consider adaptive batch_align per-sla (e.g., 4 for sub-50ms SLOs).

ashley: good catch. added adaptive_batch_align flag locally and re-ran — p50 improved by ~6% for low-latency routes without touching p99.

maria: what's the recommended runbook for devs who want to try these profiles?

ashley: copy/paste checklist: 
1) enable feature flag: quant-selector-v2 on the route
2) attach quant_profile: field-sweep-2026-03
3) set selector.min_switch_uptime_ms >= 2000 for production
4) monitor perf-bot alerts and kv_copy_rate (>0.05 is warning)
5) if kv_copy spikes, flip to prefer-compatible-kv kernel or tighten hysteresis.

perf-bot: metric snapshot: kv_copy_rate=0.042, avg_hysteresis_ms=310, selector_switches_per_min=0.9

sam: ok will try enabling on staging for llama routes tomorrow. can we also add an automated trace that captures the kernel transition + kv copy stack so SREs can triage faster?

jin: I can add a lightweight marker in the runtime that emits a single-line csv: ts,route,model,old_kernel,new_kernel,kv_copy_bytes,latency_ms. low overhead.

ashley: that would be great. jin, can you PR the marker and the perf-bot parser to alert when kv_copy_bytes > 1MB or latency delta > 20%?

jin: on it.

maria: thanks all. ashley — please open a short RFC with the findings and paste these numbers. also include the config snippet and the rollout plan. i'll coordinate with product for the canary.

ashley: will do, filing RFC now and linking here when ready. :raised_hands:

devex: one last note — we should surface a short 'recommended profile' YAML in the console for Llama/Mistral/Qwen so users don't have to hand edit. i'll start a mock for console.

ashley: perfect, thanks everyone.
